claims.text: The as-built additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an FCC matrix.
The twin density of this alloy can be systematically varied through additive-manufacturing processing parameters.
A high density of twin boundaries creates nanoscale elastic-field undulations.
Twin-associated elastic-field undulations have characteristic wavelengths of approximately 1–2 nm.
Elastic-field undulations locally lower the nucleation barrier for oxide or reduced-phase precipitates during high-temperature gas exposure.
Twin boundaries are preferential nucleation sites for oxidation- or reduction-induced phase transformations.
Twin-induced elastic undulations enhance local chemical reactivity and catalyze oxide or reduced-phase formation.
Localized oxide or reduced-phase precipitates induce stress concentrations.
Precipitate-induced stress concentrations accelerate crack initiation and propagate catastrophic failure.
Reducing twin density delays degradation and catastrophic failure.
High-twin-density specimens will nucleate oxide or reduction-induced phases earlier and more locally along twin boundaries than low-twin-density specimens.
High-twin-density specimens will initiate cracks earlier and reach catastrophic failure sooner than low-twin-density specimens.
Low-twin-density specimens will exhibit more spatially uniform and delayed degradation.
The proposed comparison is between deliberately prepared high- and low-twin-density specimens exposed at 750 °C under controlled oxidizing and reducing atmospheres.
In-situ TEM can be used to measure the timing and spatial distribution of oxide or reduced-phase nucleation and crack initiation during the exposure.
EBSD and atom-probe tomography can confirm twin density and establish that twin density is the independent variable.
The proposed mechanism applies around 750 °C in controlled oxidizing or reducing gas environments.
Markedly different temperatures or environments may activate different degradation mechanisms.
The relative contribution of twin density versus other microstructural defects is uncertain.
No statistically significant difference in phase-formation kinetics or crack-initiation time between high- and low-twin-density specimens would falsify the proposed governing role of twin boundaries.
